findings.description: The security group permits TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0 and is attached to an instance in a public subnet with an internet gateway default route, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet for brute-force and exploitation attempts.
The egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, removing any outbound network boundary and easing data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised host.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and the user_data installs only a plain Apache HTTP listener with no TLS anywhere in the configuration, so portal traffic traverses the internet in cleartext.

The user_data script exports a static AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in cleartext. User data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process on the host (or via SSRF) and through ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, leaking long-lived IAM credentials instead of using an instance profile.

No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so token-optional IMDSv1 remains enabled on an internet-facing web server, allowing SSRF-based retrieval of the user_data secrets and any instance credentials.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is declared, so the root EBS volume is not guaranteed to be encrypted at rest (dependent on AMI and account default-encryption settings).

The instance launches into a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true whose route table has a 0.0.0.0/0 route to the internet gateway, placing the host directly on the internet with no load balancer, bastion, or private-subnet segmentation.
The attached data volume does not set encrypted = true or a kms_key_id, so data written to the portal server's disk is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot derives from an unencrypted volume and is therefore unencrypted itself, persisting cleartext data that can be copied or shared across accounts.

The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration or KMS key), so network telemetry is stored without enforced encryption.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or restrictive bucket policy is defined for the flow-log bucket, leaving it reliant on account-level defaults as the only guard against accidental public exposure of network flow data.
No bucket policy denies requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so flow log objects may be written or read over unencrypted HTTP.
force_destroy = true with no versioning or object lock on the audit/flow-log bucket allows stored network telemetry to be deleted while non-empty, undermining log integrity and forensic availability.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance launched in this subnet automatically receives a public IP, defeating network segmentation by default.
